findings.text: follow-on: a generic cache-path helper is reached from serve.py and compliance.py through an underscore-private symbol owned by the metadata-index module, so the capability's owner is not discoverable from the call site and a future third cache would have to know to import metadata_index.

item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is one path owner for the four config-home caches that includes the writer's format; reckon/metadata_index.py:1075 _persisted_cache_path appends -v{version} and reckon/serve.py:1556, reckon/serve.py:1935 and reckon/compliance.py:139 route all four caches through it.

justifications.durability: tests/test_cache_paths_carry_their_format.py:102 asserts rebuilds == {1: 1, 2: 1} and reddens under the negative control, and :72 asserts paths[1] != paths[2] and reddens at the extracted base, so two independent assertions each fail if the format leaves the path.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_cache_paths_carry_their_format.py runs the alternating-writer case for each of the four caches, and its head, base and negative-control results are recorded in the manifest and the head-cache-formats and base-cache-formats logs.
justifications.fit: the helper is named by mechanism at reckon/metadata_index.py:1075 and follows the private cross-module import already used at reckon/serve.py:327.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/metadata_index.py:1075-1085 is called by reckon/serve.py:1556, reckon/serve.py:1935 and reckon/compliance.py:139, so all four named caches take their path from the one format-suffixed owner.
